newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Lamfalussy says sees flexible 2-year ERM rule.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy says sees flexible 2-year ERM rule.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) head Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Tuesday he could imagine a country would not have to be linked to the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) for two years before joining the European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Asked if it was too late for Italy and Finland to join EMU at its start in 1999 since they would not have been members of ERM for two years, Lamfalussy said: "I can imagine that they would interpret it flexibly, but I don't know."
He was in Sweden to address parliament in a public session on Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
The Maastricht Treaty says a country must be an ERM participant two years prior to the decision on which countries join EMU.
However, others argue that membership is not that important provided a country fulfils all the other Maastricht criteria on inflation, deficits and debt.
Italy was ejected from ERM in 1992 so a strict reading of the criterion would disqualify it from EMU from its scheduled start in 1999.
The Finnish markka was linked to ERM in October 1996, so by end-1998 it will not have been in the ERM for the required two years either.
